recipes.name: Easy Baked Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Season pork chops with garlic powder and seasoning salt. Place beaten eggs in a small bowl. Dredge pork chops lightly in flour; dip into beaten egg, then press into bread crumbs to coat both sides.
Heat oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat. Add breaded pork chops and cook until golden brown, about 5 minutes per side; transfer to a 9x13-inch baking dish and cover tightly with foil.
Bake in the preheated oven for 35 to 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix condensed soup, milk, and white wine in a medium bowl until smooth.
Pour soup mixture over pork chops.
Replace the foil, and continue to bake for another 10 to 15 minutes, or until pork chops are tender and an instant-read thermometer inserted near the bone reads at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).
Let rest briefly. Serve hot and enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Baked Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: These easy baked pork chops turn out juicy and tender — plus they are quick to prep with simple ingredients for a family-friendly weeknight dinner.

video.description: Every home chef needs a baked pork chop recipe that is quick and easy, just like the one in this video. You may have all the ingredients already in the house. Try serving over rice.

review.reviewBody: I took some advice from pervious reviewers and made sure that I fried the chops until the outside was very crispy (make sure the oil is hot before adding the chops, makes a difference in how tender they turn out). I also doubled the gravy, and used 1 can cream of mushroom and 1 can golden mushroom. That really helped keep the dish from having that "some kind of meat covered w/cream of mushroom soup" taste. I also sauteed some fresh mushrooms in the pan I'd cooked the pork in and added them to the soup mixture. I added some extra garlic and just a couple dashes of cayenne. I cooked the chops for 20/20.....needed less cooking time I think cause I'd browned them so well. Turned out wonderful!

I intended to submit this review two weeks ago & since then, my husband has requested this dish three more times. I did change a couple things. I baked for 35 minutes and warmed the sauce in a pot on the stove rather than pouring it over the chops. I also used cream of chicken rather than mushroom, since we're not mushroom fans and doubled the milk rather than using wine. It turned out fabulous. THANKS so much for this recipe!
I used apple juice instead of white wine and these were superb!
I added carrots and fresh sliced mushrooms. I deglazed with white wine and substituted chicken broth for milk. Finished in the LeCreuset at 350 for 75 minutes.

I’ve tried this recipe twice. It has really good flavoring, but cooking it for an hour and a half dried the pork out despite using the thick cuts of meat. If there is a next time, I will use a meat thermometer and adjust cooking time as needed.

I made it with cream of celery since one household member is not a fan of mushrooms. I used a 12" cast iron skillet to brown the chops and just pop that in the oven, covered, for the baking. One less pan to clean. Cast iron loves recipes like this!! This is the only pork chop recipe I've tried that doesn't end up like shoe leather.

I made for the first time last night. Didn't have cream of mushroom so used cream of chicken. My chops were not thick so I cut back on the cooking time. Put in the oven for about 25 minutes, then again with the sauce for 15 minutes. They were SO tender!! My husband who is not a chop fan, loved them!!

*DISCLOSURE* I DID NOT PUT THE SAUCE ON THE CHOPS DUE TO LACTOSE INTOLERANT HUBBY!! The pork chops were absolutely delish! I will happily make them again. I finished in the air fryer to crisp them up. The sauce made on the stovetop was “meh,” a bit tasteless. I will not be making the sauce next time.
I followed directions for the pork chops and used an iron skillet….it was so good….this was an easy recipe….though I didn’t cook as long as directed…
1 ½ hours is WAAAAYY too long in the oven!! They are dried out after just 30 mins, given that the outsides have already been exposed to heat in the frying pan. I will NOT be following this recipe!

Best porkchops I’ve ever made and I make good chops!
I cut down the initial bake time from one hour to 40 minutes and use chicken broth instead of wine.
Made them several times now and am a big fan.
Great recipe! East & fairly quick. Dinner guests loved it as did I.
One of our favorite meals to make but we always double the sauce to soak in the rice! So yummy!
I used Peppercorn Country time Gravy & it is a HIT!!!!

Excellent recipe. I have made it several times. The only minor tweaks I have made is to use Italian-style panko bread crumbs which I personally prefer in any recipe over regular bread crumbs and one part dry sherry to two parts white wine. This is a down home but gourmet recipe.
Added sliced button mushrooms to the sauce.

Using the recipe for frying, I was very impressed with myself as I don't fry often and I don't get that perfect crisp brown outcome. I did this time. I took others opinions and made the gravy separate and then poured it on top as I served. I was afraid of putting the chops in the oven, covered with no moisture. Would they burn? Dry out? They weren't completely cooked through so I guess they would have been ok but I ended up putting a teaspoon of broth at the bottom of the pan before putting into the oven. The chops were tender but a bit "moist", the outside was soft and coating came off easily. My mistake I guess but I wanted to mention Incase anyone else was thinking the same as I had. Other than that it was a very good meal. I also used boneless chops and baked for 30 min. Next time I will do thicker bone-in.
This was a great pork chop, easy weeknight alternative to chicken/beef staples. will make again!
I did not use white wine because I didn’t have any and I used thin cut boneless chops. Very good.
Very good and very close to our own family recipe, thank you! Not a regular wine drinker, I sometimes substitute for a tiny bit of Marsala wine or broth.
